items.summary: Five FIRs have been registered across Karnataka over alleged attempts to delete voters from electoral rolls through bulk Form 7 applications during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). These FIRs have been filed in the wake of strong objection to the use of Form 7 to allegedly disenfranchise Muslims on a mass scale. The FIRs have been registered in Belagavi, Bidar and Mysuru districts following complaints alleging the use of false information, forged documents and applications submitted without the knowledge of voters. The cases have been filed under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, forgery, impersonation and criminal conspiracy. Chief Electoral Officer for Karnataka V Anbu Kumar said in a press release that although 84,900 Form 7s had been received, the ECI had not taken anyone off the electoral rolls. He also said ECI officials had been directed to take action against those who had “knowingly made false claims” while filing Form 6, Form 6A, Form 7, and Form 8, under Section 31 of the Representation of People’s Act after conducting inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules. items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. At least five workers were killed and more than 10 others injured after a boiler exploded at the TIL Healthcare Private Limited, a pharmaceutical company located in Sri City Special Economic Zone (SEZ), in Tirupati district. The incident occurred at around 8 am on Saturday, October 3 when workers were engaged in the morning shift at the manufacturing unit. An explosion triggered a fire, leaving several workers injured. The injured were rushed to a hospital within the Sri City premises for treatment. While initial reports put the death toll at four, Tirupati Superintendent of Police (SP) L Subbarayudu later confirmed that five people had died. Two workers died at the spot, while others succumbed to their injuries during treatment. Three victims have been identified as Gourab Roy (35), Chinna Mastan (36) and Ramesh (40). Vasu (36), who was critically injured in the blast, died while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Chennai, reports said. The facts, simply put, are as follows: a private university encroached upon government land in Tamil Nadu, which had been allotted to the State Prison Department for an open prison. The Madras High Court ordered eviction of the private university from the encroached land. The private university has challenged the said order before the Supreme Court. During the course of the hearing, the Court suggested the State government should avoid demolishing the private university buildings and repossessing the land. Instead, it suggested that the private university should: (i) identify and provide suitable land (ii) bear the cost of purchasing land identified by the government or (iii) should pay the market price (or more than that) to the government for the land that they encroached. The Supreme Court mentioned that they are concerned because the State repossessing the land will result in the demolition of an education institution. items.title: Over 2 lakh Telangana voters received SIR notices without reason cited: Study
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. More than two lakh voters in Telangana have received notices as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls with no mention of what discrepancy prompted the action. According to an analysis of election data by the Sabar Institute and the Constitutional Guardians Forum, 2.01 lakh electors (2,01,249) were issued notices with the “reason for discrepancy” field left blank. The analysis examined 92.85 lakh discrepancy notices, which make up 31.3% of the state’s electorate. The largest category was voters classified as ‘unmapped with last SIR’, accounting for 32.37 lakh (34.9%) notices. Another 25.97 lakh (28%) notices related to a mismatch in the parent’s name. Self-name mismatches accounted for 11.14 lakh notices. The notices issued were particularly high in constituencies bordering Hyderabad. Quthbullapur recorded notices for 66.6% of its electorate, followed by Kukatpally at 65.4%, Uppal at 57%, Medchal at 56%, and Serilingampally at 55.8%. items.title: One Nation, One Election: Supreme Court says no parliamentary panel meeting with CJI, judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India has said that no meeting will take place between its judges and the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the 'One Nation, One Election' bills. According to PTI , the JPC dropped the plan to meet top court judges after the opposition raised objections to the same. Earlier, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal had revealed at a press conference that the JPC was scheduled to hold discussions with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and other apex court judges on October 6. The JPC, chaired by BJP Member of Parliament PP Chaudhary, is examining the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024. The two bills seek to put in place a framework for holding Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections together. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal Sibal termed the proposed interaction unprecedented and unconstitutional. He said that a parliamentary committee briefing sitting judges on a bill, even before finalising its report, has never happened in India's history. He added that this goes against the principle of separation of powers among the executive, the legislature and the judiciary. Parliament makes laws
